clue.text: Invalid has tube, initially that is, inserted to breathe

indicators.note: something inserted is put inside another word, here the one for gasping

parts.note: to pant is to breathe hard

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of tube
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A sick person on a ward has a tube fitted to help them breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' tempts as the adjective meaning not valid; it is the noun for a sick person. 'Initially' acts on tube alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An invalid, stressed on the first syllable, is a sick person, and a sick person under care is a patient.

clue.text: Satisfied after fruit drop

indicators.note: after means the first word given is placed behind the second in the answer

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
a demand that is satisfied has been met

explanation.surface: Someone is contented once the fruit has fallen from the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply, the same as to drop like a stone.

clue.text: Try on suit for sporting event

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first word sits on top of the next one

parts.note: to test is to try out
to suit something is to match it

explanation.surface: Trying on an outfit to wear to a big sporting occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: A test match is an international cricket (or rugby) match between national sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is an international fixture, a major contest in cricket or rugby, so a sporting event.

clue.text: Had dinner with some bloke at Enzo's

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across bloke, at and Enzo

explanation.surface: Someone dined with a man at an Italian restaurant called Enzo's.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten is the past participle: 'I have had dinner' and 'I have eaten' say the same thing.

clue.text: One draws on people from Edinburgh Festival event and its organisation

parts.note: the Edinburgh Military Tattoo is a famous display held during the festival

indicators.note: organisation is the act of arranging, so these letters get put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist from the Edinburgh Festival, drawing on its organisers for material.
explanation.walkthrough: A military tattoo is an evening display of military music and marching, the Edinburgh one held at the castle each August.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist literally draws designs in ink on people's skin, a cryptic twist on drawing on people for inspiration.

clue.text: Acted to deceive in plot

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the following one

parts.note: a plot of garden is a bed
to have someone, as in 'you've been had', is to deceive them

explanation.surface: Someone played a part in order to deceive, as part of a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' reads as a conspiracy, but it is the gardener's sense, a patch of ground for planting.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave is to act or conduct oneself in a particular way, so the past tense matches acted.

clue.text: Sad son squanders money

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
s is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father is unhappy that his boy is wasting cash.
explanation.walkthrough: To blue money is British slang for spending it recklessly; blues is the verb's third person.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to blue cash is to waste it, so someone who blues it squanders money.

clue.text: Good exam results for senior boys?

definitions.text: Good exam results for senior boys?

parts.note: surface reading: top scores in a test
setter's reading: older lads who share a common boy's name, the tall ones

explanation.walkthrough: High marks are good exam scores; read as a name, Mark, and high as tall or senior, they are also older boys called Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent scores in an exam are described as high marks, the phrase that also names lofty boys called Mark.

clue.text: Very unknown at home, German's competing

parts.note: v is the abbreviation for very
y is one of the algebra letters for an unknown quantity
someone at home is in
G is the abbreviation for German; the 's stands for is, joining to the definition

explanation.surface: A little-known German, staying in, is taking part in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete, so vying means competing for something.

clue.text: Journal contains time after note about what one eats

indicators.note: contains says the first word holds the others inside it

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

indicators.note: after says the time letter follows the note letter in the order written

parts.note: E is a musical note
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A food diary records, after each note, the time of every meal.
explanation.walkthrough: E then T go inside DIARY after its second letter: DI-ET-ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary means relating to diet, the food a person habitually consumes.

clue.text: Furore raised by Gogglebox?

parts.note: something raised is up
goggle-box is British slang for a television set

explanation.surface: A row stirred up by the TV show Gogglebox, where people are filmed watching television.
explanation.walkthrough: Gogglebox is also a British reality show, which makes the surface plausible; here it is just the TV set.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a disturbance or commotion, a fuss of the same kind as a furore.

clue.text: Holiday rep arranged ride out around the middle of August

indicators.note: around has the rearranged letters wrap themselves about the central pair
arranged means the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the middle of keeps only the central pair of letters of the six-letter word

parts.note: the two central letters of August

explanation.surface: A holiday rep organised a trip out in mid-August.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday rep often leads excursions, and a tour guide is the person who shows visitors around.

clue.text: Doctor, doctor! One must be serious!

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the next words are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The old 'Doctor, doctor!' joke opening, with a stern warning that this time it's no laughing matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'Doctor' does two jobs: the first is the noun MO, the second the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A momentous matter is one of great importance, grave and weighty, so serious.

clue.text: Mum's eating good hot stuff!

indicators.note: eating has the first word swallow the next one inside it

parts.note: mama is another word for mum
g is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Mum is tucking in, and the food is good and very hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is molten rock beneath the earth's crust, literally extremely hot material.

clue.text: Teach to prepare trout

indicators.note: preparing fish means cutting and working it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cookery lesson on how to get a fish ready for the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to give private instruction, a synonym for the verb teach.

clue.text: Get leader redeployed and demoted

indicators.note: redeployed means moved to new positions, so the letters are placed differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Office politics: the boss is moved to another post and dropped down the ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegated means moved to a lower rank or division, which is being demoted.

clue.text: Popular company has top grade lines in place to get better

parts.note: something in fashion is in
a firm is a business company
A is the top grade in many marking schemes
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: A popular company boasts a top-rated railway network, as places to improve go.
explanation.definitionFit: An infirmary is a hospital, where patients are cared for until they recover.

clue.text: Inspire Jo to be a rebel

parts.note: to fire someone up is to inspire them
Jo Brand is a well-known British comedian

explanation.surface: Encouraging a girl named Jo to turn rebellious.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo Brand is a British stand-up comedian, so her first name stands for her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is a person who stirs up trouble or passionately champions a cause, an agitator.

clue.text: Random treat but I get credit

indicators.note: random means in no fixed order, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone does a random good deed for others but takes the praise for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to a person is to credit them with it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cover chair with high armrest

parts.note: something high is up
read as arm-rest, a place where a firearm rests: a gun holster

explanation.surface: Furnishing advice: put fabric on a chair with tall armrests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armrest' looks like part of the chair; split as arm (a weapon) and rest, it is a holster.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to fit a chair or sofa with padding and a fabric covering.

clue.text: Modernised university has personal digital assistant initially taking notes

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: initially says to take opening letters from the words around it

parts.note: the first letters of the three words
the first letter of taking
E and D are musical notes

explanation.surface: A university now has handheld gadgets for students to take notes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Updated means brought up to date, made current, which is what modernised describes.

clue.text: Model in sari playing Indian instrument

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the rearranged letters
playing suggests the letters are played about with and reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: A model in traditional Indian dress performs on an Indian instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked string instrument from India.

clue.text: Give seat once more to dance partner at court

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
in bridge East is partner to West, abbreviated E
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: At a royal court ball, a dancer offers a chair again to a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is played in pairs, North with South and East with West, so a partner can be any compass letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elect someone is to vote them back into office, giving them their parliamentary seat again.

clue.text: Hound about home-making

indicators.note: about has the first word go round the second

parts.note: a hound is a dog
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A dog fussing around a domestic task, as dogs underfoot do.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'home-making' is a trick: 'home' belongs to the wordplay and 'making' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing and making are both general verbs for carrying out or producing, as in doing or making a cake.

clue.text: Often an incident arising's a bit absurd

indicators.note: in a down clue, arising means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top
a bit means only a small part of the words before it is used

parts.note: the letters run across often, an and incident

explanation.surface: Things that crop up often are rather ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or pointless, a close synonym for absurd.

clue.text: Vegetable from Aube region cooked with nothing removed

indicators.note: cooked means prepared and changed, so the letters are mixed up
removed means that letter is taken away from the rest

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A French recipe: a vegetable from the Aube department cooked on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: Aube is a department of north-east France, which makes a French dish plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine is the British name for the eggplant, a purple vegetable.

clue.text: Getting help to acquire credit is bitter

indicators.note: to acquire is to take something in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: aid is help
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Having to ask for financial help to get a loan leaves a sour taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and harsh to taste or smell, which is bitter.

clue.text: Agrees, even, to support artist's violent passions

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support means placed underneath the next word

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: even means only the letters in even-numbered places, second, fourth and sixth, are kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone even agrees to back a painter's furious outbursts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rages are fits of violent anger, intense outbursts of feeling.

clue.text: Man races to catch rodent before old atmosphere returns in restaurant

indicators.note: before says the next piece comes after what precedes it
to catch is to hold, so the first item is wrapped round the next

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) motorcycle races are held on the Isle of Man
a rat is a rodent
o is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: returns means the word goes back the way it came, read right to left

parts.note: air is atmosphere

explanation.surface: A man hurries to catch a rat in a restaurant before the old ambience comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man, home of the TT races.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eating house, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Dressing for matador's wounds reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: a matador is wounded when a bull gores him; in a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: Bandages needed for a bullfighter's injuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauze is the thin open-weave fabric used as a wound dressing.

clue.text: Feared becoming red and dead!

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so the letters change their order

parts.note: the two words red and dead, joined by and, are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A frightening fate: turning red and then dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreaded means regarded with great fear, which is what feared describes.

clue.text: Drop of French perfume

parts.note: de is French for of
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: A drop of French perfume, as a dab behind the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' reads as a tiny amount of scent, but it is the definition: a fall or downward slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a downward slope or fall, the noun sense of drop.
